approved: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2014

Brendan O'Connor I move the opposition amendment to the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2014, as circulated under my name: (1) Schedule 2, page 28 (after line 15), after item 58, insert: 58A Guidelines The amendments to section 65 of the FMA Act made by this Schedule do not affect the continuity of the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines 2012, as in force immediately before the commencement time. As I said earlier in my contribution to the debate on these bills, the opposition has grave concerns about the impact of the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines and their potential impact upon cleaners' rates of pay going forward. In this place we had the Prime Minister, when questions were put to him on this matter during question time, give an unqualified guarantee that cleaners who work under Commonwealth contracts would not lose any payment or suffer any loss to or reductions of their hourly rate of pay. If this amendment is not supported by the government, those unqualified statements will be found to be untrue. The only issue is whether the Prime Minister intentionally misled this parliament by answering as he did the questions asked of him about the impact on cleaners under Commonwealth contracts. As the member for Watson and the member for Bendigo have said in this debate, the repeal of this guideline will mean that, when future contracts are tendered, those tendering will be able—if they are successful—to reduce the rates of pay for cleaners under that contract by almost $5 an hour. That is what would happen to cleaners as a result of the provision contained within this bill. For that reason, and so that we can ensure that the Prime Minister did not mislead this place in question time when asked about this matter, we would expect the government to support this amendment. Introduced the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2014, which would amend more than 250 Commonwealth acts to implement the PGPA Act from 1 July 2014, replacing the Financial Management and Accountability Act and the Commonwealth Authorities and Companies Act.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability bills and related appropriation bills through the House before the end of the financial year, noting the usual longer period for consideration had not been possible this time.

Raised concerns that a bill titled 'public governance' was being rushed through without proper scrutiny, noting it would impact around 250 pieces of legislation and countless Commonwealth regulations.

Explained that the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act would replace the Financial Management and Accountability Act and Commonwealth Authorities and Companies Act from 1 July 2014, and that the consequential bill fixes drafting errors in Labor's original legislation that went unnoticed during its passage.

Moved a formal Labor amendment to preserve the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines within the bill, arguing that voting it down would prove the Prime Minister misled Parliament when he guaranteed no cleaner's pay would be cut.

Explained that the government would not oppose Labor's amendment to ensure the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act commences on schedule from 1 July 2014, describing it as the most significant change to public sector governance in about 17 years, amending more than 250 pieces of Commonwealth legislation.

Supported an amendment protecting Clean Start pay rates for cleaners, saying the government's own bill this week would have let cleaners' pay fall from $22.02 an hour to the equivalent of $17.49, a loss of up to $344 a week, despite the Prime Minister's assurance that no cleaner's pay would be cut.
